name: enable-saved-custom-unit-combat
reason: User-requested recovery of deferred non-3D saved-custom-unit combat work: exact authoritative admission, immutable construction snapshots, replay/recovery and fog proof, and campaign picker/readiness integration. Excludes model and tactical presentation work. Reviewed 2026-09-15 against exact main 4d7d17c3d (the merge commit of PR #1713) using the consolidated S6 receipt openspec/planning/2026-09-12-roadmap-completion/evidence/r2-combat-s6-consolidated-20260915.json: all five of the roadmap node R2.combat acceptance lines are satisfied with recorded exit codes and log hashes (13 suites / 69 tests, typecheck / lint / format:check / build / openspec strict all exit 0, e2e saved-custom-combat 1 passed first attempt against the hydrated standalone production server). Three of the six task rows are now checked - the strict projection / catalog endpoint / picker merge row, the shared catalog admission row (S5 PRs #1712 and #1713, 11 mutations with no survivors), and the verification row. Reviewed again 2026-09-15 (batch 3): the redaction row ("recovery streams") is now closed too - PR #1726 8c8f8221c4 mutation-proves recovered-host delivery redaction through a real DurableMatchStore cold reopen, so four of six rows are now checked. Two rows remain held open with the residual named on the row: co-op happy-path snapshot carriage is structural via EncounterService rather than asserted; and the "rewind" clause, recorded as owner decision OD-rewind-branch-reader, is structurally unreachable for any match stream on the current head (the journal mirror appends onto the baseline branch id while the match-store segment reader serves only root) and belongs to adopt-combat-journal-cutover-and-gm-rewind. Two declared boundaries carried on the verification row: the production combat launch belongs to R2.combat-browser (now separately proven by PR #1731 392c207de7, a saved custom unit launching into production combat with no canonical substitution - not claimed as closing this row's own text), and every build proven on main for either row still carries the E2E public flags, so a flag-free vanilla production build has still never been run separately.
